A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FREE-Merging research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and expanded presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging experiments across vision, language and multimodal tasks, with ablations and additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds frequency-domain diagnostics, expanded component ablations, method-combination experiments and expert-output similarity results.

M1.justification: Equations 1–4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same filtering, merging coefficients, expert extraction, rescaling and routing procedure. Section 6.6 additionally introduces evaluated combinations of FR-Merging with Ties-Merging, Breadcrumbs and TSVM, constituting limited hybrid variants.

E1.justification: The vision, GLUE, PEFT, instruction-following, mathematics, coding and multimodal datasets and tasks are retained. The new Flan-T5 diagnostics and RoBERTa generalization analysis use already covered GLUE tasks; they change model configurations and analyses without adding datasets, domains or populations.

E2.justification: v2 adds TSVM as an evaluated comparator in Table 8. Its new loss-landscape comparison includes Top-K retention and DARE alongside FR-Merging (Figure 9), whereas v1's landscape comparison used Weight Averaging and FR-Merging. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation procedures relating frequency-amplitude variance to normalized merging accuracy, inspecting layer spectra, and measuring expert-output CKA similarity. Table 7 expands component controls and evaluates three ViT variants instead of v1 Table 6's single variant. Appendix D also introduces Flan-T5 diagnostics and a loss-landscape comparison retaining the top 20% of parameters.

E4.justification: New analyses examine frequency-domain interference across models and layers, combinations with other merging methods, Top-K/DARE loss landscapes, language-model generalization, and rescaling's effect on output similarity. Component ablations are substantially expanded. The existing router, cutoff-frequency, non-overlapping-parameter and expert-construction analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added frequency-amplitude variance measures differences among models, not uncertainty across repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores and detailed appendix results are retained, but substantial diagnostic and ablation results are added. Examples include Table 1's amplitude variance of 0.059 for Task Arithmetic versus 0.045 for FR-Merging, and Table 12's ViT-B/32 CKA increase from 0.5314 without scaling to 0.8484 with scaling. The FR-plus-coefficients ablation changes from 77.64 in v1 to 78.10 in v2. The baseline row also changes from labelled Weight Averaging at 65.80 to an unnamed all-disabled configuration at 70.10, which cannot establish a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: The theorem, its assumptions and complete appendix proof are unchanged apart from renumbering. The method equations and complexity derivation are also retained. New frequency-domain arguments are explanatory and empirical rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes removing task-specific low-frequency information that harms generalization. v2's abstract and contribution list instead foreground a claimed first identification of frequency-domain task interference and argue that existing spatial-domain approaches cannot adequately address it. This substantially redefines the central scientific contribution while retaining the efficiency and expert-module claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mechanism in which stronger frequency components overshadow weaker task signals, interprets amplitude variance as interference, and argues that FR-Merging complements existing methods. Appendix D adds explanations involving parameter redundancy, rescaling-induced output preservation and possible training-path effects on amplitude clustering. It also qualifies filtering's impact as weaker for language models than for vision models.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies the frequency coordinates used in Equation 2 and specifies 20% parameter retention for the new Top-K landscape comparison. Existing hardware disclosures and experiment-configuration references are retained. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around interference overlooked by spatial-domain merging methods and supports that comparison with a dedicated section and table. It adds citations including TSVM, BitDelta, binary task switching, MetaGPT and Flan-T5, while removing the earlier importance-estimation pruning reference. Existing backbone/expert comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method motivation and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. A new frequency-interference section reorganizes the argument, router analysis moves into the ablation section, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. The title and terminology also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds frequency-distribution and correlation plots, extensive layerwise figure grids, a combined landscape/generalization figure, and transferability and CKA tables. The component-ablation table is redesigned with explicit component switches and three model columns. Existing figures and benchmark tables are largely retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new diagnostics, expanded component controls and CKA analysis strengthen empirical support for filtering and expert rescaling. The revised ablation also aligns its FR-plus-coefficients score with the retained benchmark result. These gains are tempered by sparse descriptions of the new diagnostic protocols and an attribution inconsistency: Appendix D.1 describes Flan-T5 results, while Figure 6's caption names ViT-B/32. The overall improvement is useful but limited.
